findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.java line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with zero arguments, but the only definition in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm.java takes a UserModel argument: protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). There is no zero-arg overload. The module will fail to compile, so nothing in this PR can build or ship.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys disabled on initial login where user is null
findings.body: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate previously called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when passkeys were enabled and no user was selected, which is the normal first-login conditional-UI case. The new code gates it with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null. When context.getUser() is null on the initial login page the method returns false, so no challenge, no ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute and no passkeys data are prepared. Usernameless/discoverable-key login on the first page is broken; the existing tests expect form[@id='webauth'] to be present on initial login.

findings.title: Error challenge drops passkeys setup for initial login
findings.body: The overridden challenge(context, error, field) changed from if (context.getUser() == null && webauthn enabled) to if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())), which is only true when context.getUser() != null. On the initial login where the user is still unknown, a failed username/password attempt will re-render the login form without calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm, so conditional passkeys disappear after the first error. The correct condition must allow passkeys regardless of whether a user is already selected, not invert the old user==null case to user!=null.
